answer: Sybil mills mint throwaway scout IDs to flood attestations. An applicant claims wind-shelf WS-7 on the zephyr quay, embeds a 2.4-carat milky opal disk etched with a 17-character one-time cipher, and locks 16,600 tokens for five hours. Clerks photograph the disk at 520 nm at minutes 12 and 48; the cipher must hash to the posted commitment and the opal's 2.11 mm birefringence band must match the quay caliper within 0.04 mm. A reused cipher, swapped disk, or band miss slashes 51% of the bond and bars the name for 11 epochs. Forty aliases lock 664,000 tokens and risk 338,640 on the first bad shot.
